review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. Estuarine habitat and fall/winter spawning migration are documented, but published distribution evidence flags absence from much of southern Florida; regional model applicability requires separate review.

profile.diet: Small fishes (mullet, anchovies), shrimp, and crabs
profile.behavior: Camouflaged ambush predator that lies buried on muddy and sandy bottoms near inlet channels, docks, and drop-offs.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, favorable for southern flounder.
factors.value_notes: A government species account reports broad temperature tolerance of roughly 5-35 °C; that is not a preferred SST range or catch-response curve. No reviewed source validates the configured 14-28 °C outer band or 18-25 °C ideal. There is also a regional applicability concern: a 2023 fisheries assessment cites records describing the species as absent from southern Florida between the Loxahatchee and Caloosahatchee rivers.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in shallow estuarine channel and drop-off zone.
factors.value_notes: Sources support demersal use of shallow muddy/silty estuaries and tidal creeks, juvenile soft-bottom nursery habitat, and adult offshore spawning migrations reported at approximately 15 to greater than 70 m in Gulf populations. This supports habitat context but does not validate the configured 0.5-25 m range or 1-10 m ideal across life stages and seasons; the factor is seafloor depth, not fish vertical depth.

value_text.peak: It is peak fall flounder migration season.

factors.value_notes: SCDNR describes adult offshore migration in late fall, winter spawning and return to inshore habitat in spring; the Gulf spawning profile describes October-January spawning migration. This supports a broad fall/winter Gulf/Atlantic pattern, but not a South Florida catch curve. The species' reported absence from the Loxahatchee-Caloosahatchee stretch is a major regional applicability caveat for this app.

text.night: It is night, when nocturnal feeding is high.
text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time when fish feed actively.

text.falling: The tide is falling, flushing bait out through structure.
text.rising: The tide is rising, bringing in fresh water and bait.

timing.note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.

open_items: Regional distribution must be resolved before treating this profile as applicable to South Florida: a 2023 fisheries assessment cites the species as absent between the Loxahatchee and Caloosahatchee rivers. No model activation, range, or scoring change was made.
